findings.claim: The encounter treated as negligible becomes an unavoidable confrontation, and those who left it aside are themselves placed outside regard.

Liqāʾ carries face-to-face encounter; nasītum makes that meeting the object of deliberate leaving, while nasīnākum reverses the participants and activates the discarded-object image through the same root and the first-person/second-person contrast.
findings.reader_payoff: The judgment reads as a reversal of social regard: the neglected meeting returns, and its neglecters are left aside.
findings.containment: The discarded-object image is an attributed local analogy carried by the transitive object and reversed syntax; the verbs are not claimed to name literal discarded things, and the divine verb does not mean cognitive amnesia.

epistemic.reason: The trace is legacy_unbound and exploratory; the cited word indices and roots match the focus surface, and a separate encounter object grounds the contact, so that uncertainty remains visible.
